notes: internal/intelligence/health.go:229 historySince/withinWindow convert float64 days to time.Duration without a range check. A threshold above ~106751 days (or 1e308 / +Inf, which the admin update path in health.go:176 stores without validating) overflows int64: the conversion is undefined in Go and on amd64 yields math.MinInt64, so withinWindow's window goes negative and the rule silently never fires -- the exact failure mode windowDays was added to prevent. Absurd input only, but an upper clamp alongside the `!(days > 0)` guard would close it.

internal/intelligence/health.go:78 windowDays deliberately reinterprets days<=0 as the seeded default (90/180) instead of 'window disabled'. For CLOSE_DATE_SLIPPAGE this reverses prior behaviour (a 0 window used to suppress the rule); the commit message states this and the `active` flag is the intended off switch, so it is a defensible call, but any operator relying on days:0 to mute slippage will see it start firing after deploy.

Tests genuinely exercise the change: TestDropRulesOnlyCountChangesInsideTheirWindow (89d fires / 91d quiet, plus a narrowed 7d window) and TestHistoryFetchCoversTheWidestConfiguredWindow both fail against the pre-change logic, and the windowDays fallback case asserts a fire that only happens if 0 falls back to 90. Boundary is probed at 89/91 but not exactly 90; minor.

Refactor scope (switch moved out of DealHealth into pure evaluateHealthRule) is declared in the commit message and is what makes the fix testable without a database. Diff-checked: the six non-history cases moved verbatim, only the three window-bounded rules changed behaviour (added windowDays + withinWindow + a windowDays evidence key). Evidence maps are rendered generically by web/src/components/Intelligence.tsx:14, so the new key breaks no client.

Seeded thresholds in migrations/002_sales_intelligence.sql:135-137 confirm the commit's premise (slippage days:180, both drops days:90). No migration, schema, auth, or deletion logic touched; opportunity_health_snapshots rows are append-only history, so a revert restores prior behaviour cleanly.
